question: What can a precisely specified computation accomplish?
idea: Some mathematical questions concern whether a procedure exists at all; others concern how much time or how accurate an approximation it needs. Those are different limits. This entry studies the particular computational question stated below.
why: The study of proof, mathematical languages, and the limits of what can be decided from a set of rules.

glossary.meaning: Running time bounded by a fixed power of the input size, a common notion of computational efficiency.
A mathematical statement proposed to be true but requiring proof or a counterexample.

exactClaim: Confirms the Blass–Gurevich–Shelah noncapture conjecture: consistency of a linear system over 𝔽3 defines a polynomial-time query on unordered finite structures that choiceless polynomial time with counting cannot express. A separate result shows that adding witnessed symmetric choice strictly increases expressive power. Both separations hold for the full counting formalism, allowing hereditarily finite sets of arbitrary finite rank.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
